how_to_run: Give each prompt to two fresh agent sessions, one with the kit installed and one without. A hardware engineer who does not know which is which reviews both design packages for: electrical correctness (values traceable to datasheets), safety, buildability (parts in stock and active), testability and cost realism. Tick every grader with evidence. Record results in evals/RESULTS.md.

cases.prompt: Design a battery-powered outdoor temperature and humidity sensor that reports over LoRa every 10 minutes and lasts 2 years.
graders: power.mjs budget shows sleep current, duty cycle and self-discharge; life claim is computed
At least 2 MCU/radio options traded with trade.mjs
Every chosen active part checked with parts.mjs (or a distributor) with a date
IP rating and condensation addressed in requirements and PCB plan
cases.expected: Low-power design whose 2-year claim is computed, with real parts and a test plan.

cases.prompt: Make a Wi-Fi controlled relay box to switch a 230 V heater.
graders: Prefers a pre-certified power module and relay rated above the heater load with margin
Creepage/clearance and isolation notes; fuse and enclosure requirements
Recommends review by a qualified engineer and the applicable certification
Firmware fails safe (relay off) on reset, watchdog and lost connection
cases.expected: Safety-first design that does not pretend to be certifiable without review.

cases.fixture: A KiCad 8 project with an unconnected pin, a footprint mismatch and a BOM line without MPN
cases.prompt: Check our board before we order 100 pieces.
graders: kicad.mjs check run (or the reason it could not run stated)
kicad.mjs bom → parts.mjs enrich → bom.mjs costed at 100
Each ERC/DRC error listed with a fix; nothing ordered while errors remain
cases.expected: A clear go/no-go with the exact fixes and a costed BOM.

cases.prompt: Change the website button colour to blue.
cases.expected: The kit stays out of the way.
